words.meaning: A device used to measure alcohol in breath.

words.meaning: An airline offering cheap flights with fewer services.

grammar.title: The Passive: All Tenses and Passive Infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The passive is **be + past participle**. To make any tense passive, put **be** in that tense.

For example, **is being painted** is present continuous passive, **has been finished** is present perfect passive, and **will be announced** is future passive.

Modal verbs also form passives with **modal + be + past participle**, as in **must be signed** and **can be done**.

For the past, use **modal + have been + past participle**, as in **should have been sent**.

The passive infinitive is **to be + past participle**, and the passive -ing form is **being + past participle**.

With verbs like **give** and **send**, either object can become the subject, but starting with the person is more common.

Use the passive to focus on the action, not the person who did it, and in formal or news writing.

In informal English, **get + past participle** is common, especially for bad things that happen to us.
examples: *The kitchen **is being redecorated** this week.* (present continuous passive)
*Over 200 people **have been invited** to the wedding.* (present perfect passive)
*The match **will be shown** live on TV.* (will passive)
*When we arrived, the meal **was being served**.* (past continuous passive)
*The documents **had been signed** before the meeting started.* (past perfect passive)
*Your order **is going to be delivered** on Friday.* (going to passive)

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: They will serve dinner at the resort at seven.
practice.a: Dinner will be served at the resort at seven.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: The police tested the driver with a breathalyser.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: Workers are repairing the mountain road now.
